title.en: Speed, leap, and throw on the athletics track

text.en: From a 100 m crouch start to the hop-step-jump of triple jump and the arc of a javelin, Track and Field athletics tests speed, technique, and precision.

Chapter 4 covers Track and Field athletics, governed globally by World Athletics (originally WAF/IAAF), with a standard track measuring 400 metres.
Track events include Sprints (100 m, 200 m, 400 m, hurdles, 4×100 m and 4×400 m relays), Middle Distance (800 m, 1500 m), and Long Distance (3000 m steeplechase, 5000 m, 10,000 m, marathon).
Sprinters use starting blocks with 'On your marks' and 'Set' commands; a false start leads to disqualification, and runners must stay in their designated lanes.
In relays, the baton must be passed inside the 20-metre baton exchange zone; 3000 m steeplechase includes 28 hurdle jumps and 7 water jumps.
Jumping events are Long Jump, Triple Jump (hop, step, jump), High Jump (4 m crossbar, tie-break by fewest misses), and Pole Vault (fiberglass/carbon pole, hands cannot slide up).
Throwing events are Shot Put, Discus Throw (2.5 m circle, 1.5 turns), Javelin Throw (overhand grip, must land inside sector), and Hammer Throw.
Athletics is divided into Track (running) events and Field (jumping and throwing) events.
A standard athletics track is 400 metres around.
Sprints use a crouch start; middle and long distances use a standing start and pacing.
In relay races, teammates pass the baton within the 20-metre exchange area.
Triple jump has three phases: hop, step, and jump; high jumpers clear a 4 m bar.
Discus is thrown from a 2.5 m circle, and javelin must be thrown overhand inside the landing sector.

problem.en: In a 4×100 m relay, a runner drops the baton inside the exchange zone, picks it up, and hands it over before leaving the 20 m zone. Is it legal?

why.en: The baton must be passed within the 20-metre exchange zone.

text.en: Since the handover completed inside the 20 m zone without obstructing other lanes, the exchange is valid.

why.en: Baton exchange rules require completion inside the designated zone.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between track events and field events with two examples of each.

requiredIdeas.en: Track events are running races (sprints, hurdles, relays, middle/long distance)
Field events are jumping (long, triple, high jump, pole vault) and throwing (shot put, discus, javelin, hammer)
A standard track is 400 m and relay baton exchange is 20 m

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the triple jump allows alternating feet on the hop and step (hop lands on same foot, step on opposite foot)

points.en: Track events include sprints, hurdles, relays, middle-distance, and long-distance runs on a 400 m track.
Sprinters use crouch starts; a false start causes disqualification.
Field jumping events are Long Jump, Triple Jump (hop-step-jump), High Jump, and Pole Vault.
Field throwing events are Shot Put, Discus (2.5 m circle), Javelin (600 g women's javelin), and Hammer.
